questions.question: How should a Go service handle logging?
questions.title: Logging Basics
questions.direct_answer: Log to stdout/stderr as structured JSON (log/slog, zap, zerolog) — the collector aggregates. Levels: debug/info/warn/error. Request-scoped context (request ID) on every line. NOT files — the platform handles that.

sections.title: Quick Revision
sections.content: Log to stdout/stderr as structured JSON (log/slog, zap, zerolog) — the collector aggregates. Levels: debug/info/warn/error. Request-scoped context (request ID) on every line. NOT files — the platform handles that.

sections.title: Interview Answer
sections.content:
The modern pattern (Go 1.21+ log/slog):

```go
import "log/slog"

// Setup: JSON to stdout
logger := slog.New(slog.NewJSONHandler(os.Stdout, nil))
slog.SetDefault(logger)

// Structured logs — key-value, not string formatting
slog.Info("user created",
    "user_id", 123,
    "email", "al@x.com",
)
slog.Error("db connection failed",
    "op", "loadUser",
    "err", err,
)
// Output:
// {"time":"...","level":"INFO","msg":"user created","user_id":123,"email":"al@x.com"}
```

The conventions interviewers check:
1. JSON to stdout — the platform's collector (CloudWatch, Loki, the K8s log) handles storage, search, retention
2. Structured fields (key-value), not formatted prose — searchable, filterable, machine-parseable
3. Levels with discipline: info (the normal flow), warn (recoverable), error (failed operation — needs attention)
4. Context (request ID, user, trace) on every line — the correlation that makes log-tracing possible
5. NO file logging, NO log rotation — that's the platform's job (12-factor)

The middleware integration (the HTTP pattern):
```go
func loggingMiddleware(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
    return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        start := time.Now()
        reqID := r.Header.Get("X-Request-ID")
        logger := logger.With("req_id", reqID, "method", r.Method, "path", r.URL.Path)
        next.ServeHTTP(w, r)  // the handler logs with the enriched logger
        logger.Info("request",
            "duration_ms", time.Since(start).Milliseconds(),
            "status", statusFrom(w))
    })
}
```

The libraries: log/slog (the stdlib, 1.21+ — the default choice), zap (Uber's — the performance leader), zerolog (the allocation-free), logrus (the pre-slog standard — being superseded). The library matters less than the pattern: structured, leveled, context-enriched, stdout.

sections.title: Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    APP[Go service] --> SLOG[slog JSON]
    SLOG --> STDOUT[stdout]
    STDOUT --> COL[collector: Loki / CloudWatch]
    COL --> SEARCH[searchable by req_id]
    MW[logging middleware] → CTX[req_id + duration + status]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The slog design (the stdlib's answer to the library wars): a Handler interface (where logs go + how they're formatted) + structured fields (slog.Any, slog.String — the type-safe key-value pairs) + a default logger (slog.SetDefault — the package-level drop-in). The JSON handler is the production default; the text handler the development default — the SAME code, different handlers.

The context propagation (the request-scoped logger pattern): the middleware creates the enriched logger (logger.With("req_id", id)) and stores it in the request's context; handlers retrieve and log with it. The pattern: logger.FromContext(ctx) — the context carries the logger; every log line from that request carries the same correlation. This is the Go implementation of 'structured logging with request ID' — the observable service.

The anti-patterns the question screens: log.Fatal in a handler (crashes the process on a recoverable error — Fatal is for STARTUP); the printf-into-log-strings (fmt.Sprintf in the message — the fields are the structure); the log-to-file approach (fights the platform, loses the K8s log collection, the rotation problem Go didn't need).
